items.example: I love the new gym. Also, it opens until midnight.

note.en: Fine in speaking; in formal writing prefer 'In addition'.
note.es: Vale al hablar; en escritos formales mejor «In addition».

items.example: The course is cheap. In addition, the teachers are very friendly.
The flat has a balcony as well as a small garden.

note.en: Followed by a noun or an -ing form.
note.es: Va seguido de un sustantivo o de una forma en -ing.

items.example: The tickets are cheap, and what's more, they include breakfast.
The train was late. On top of that, it started to rain.
I don't want to drive into town. Besides, parking costs a fortune.

note.en: Adds a further reason. Not the same as 'beside' (next to).
note.es: Añade otra razón. No es «beside» (al lado de).

items.example: Not only is the app free, but it also works without an internet connection.

note.en: After 'Not only' at the start, invert the verb.
note.es: Si empieza la frase con «Not only», invierte el verbo.

items.example: The office is easy to reach. Furthermore, it has free parking for staff.
The scheme reduces traffic. Moreover, it improves air quality in the centre.
In addition to this, I would be grateful if you could send me the full programme.

note.en: Handy in the formal email to add a second request.
note.es: Útil en el email formal para añadir una segunda petición.

items.example: The festival attracts thousands of tourists, not to mention hundreds of volunteers.

note.en: Adds something even bigger or more surprising.
note.es: Añade algo aún más grande o sorprendente.

items.example: Equally important, staff should be given time to learn the new system.
I like swimming. I like running too.

note.en: 'Too' goes at the end of the sentence.
note.es: «Too» va al final de la frase.

items.example: There is a pool in the hotel. There is also a small gym.
